cards.explanation: The answer is that the soldiers force Simon of Cyrene to carry the cross of Jesus. He was just passing by on his way in from the country. Then the soldiers "…forced him to carry the cross of Jesus." (Mark 15:21) Mark also tells us he was the father of Alexander and Rufus. Talk about a turn, friends: passing by one moment, carrying the cross the next.

The answer is False. The soldiers offered Jesus wine mixed with myrrh, "…but He did not take it." (Mark 15:23) Mark gives no reason, so I won't make one up. All we know is what He did and didn't do at Golgotha.

The lots decide what each soldier will take. The soldiers divided His garments "…by casting lots to decide what each of them would take." (Mark 15:24) Each man's share came down to the lots. I think that's a hard thing to read, friends, because those were His clothes.

The charge against Jesus reads THE KING OF THE JEWS. Mark says, "…the charge inscribed against Him read: THE KING OF THE JEWS." (Mark 15:26) He puts it right there in capital letters. It's the very charge, in the very words, written against Him.

The people passing by dare Jesus to come down from the cross and save Himself. Those who passed by said, "…come down from the cross and save Yourself!" (Mark 15:30) They were shaking their heads and heaping abuse on Him as they said it (Mark 15:29). That was the dare, friends.

The answer is True. The chief priests and scribes said, "Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe!" (Mark 15:32) Mark has them saying it among themselves. That's a lot of words about believing from people who weren't believing.

The answer is True. Mark says, "…even those who were crucified with Him berated Him." (Mark 15:32) That includes the two robbers on His right and left (Mark 15:27). Mark lists those passing by, the chief priests and scribes, and even the men crucified with Him.

The answer is darkness, friends. Mark says, "From the sixth hour until the ninth hour darkness came over all the land." (Mark 15:33) That's three hours of it, covering all the land. Mark just states it and doesn't say more.
The answer is Elijah. Some of those standing nearby said, "Behold, He is calling Elijah." (Mark 15:35) Jesus had cried out "Eloi, Eloi…" (Mark 15:34). Elijah is the name they gave when they heard it.
The answer is sour wine. Someone filled a sponge with sour wine, put it on a reed and held it up for Jesus to drink (Mark 15:36). Mark names it exactly, so we keep it exact, friends.

The answer is the veil. Mark says, "…the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom." (Mark 15:38) He puts it right after Jesus breathed His last (Mark 15:37). The veil was the temple's curtain, and it tore from the top to the bottom.

The answer is False. The centurion saw how Jesus breathed His last, and then said, "Truly this man was the Son of God!" (Mark 15:39) That wasn't mocking. After all those voices heaping abuse, his was a different one, friends.
The answer is Mary Magdalene. Among the women watching from a distance was Mary Magdalene (Mark 15:40). Mark also names Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.

The answer is Galilee. These women "…had followed Jesus and ministered to Him while He was in Galilee…" (Mark 15:41) Mark also says there were many other women who had come up to Jerusalem with Him. So these women had followed Him before they stood watching, friends.
